name: s3-search-scope-prefilter-is-server-built
description: S3 Outcome 2 (SRCH-001): the k-NN query must narrow candidates to the asking workspace's live authorized source scopes BEFORE ranking them. internal/search/client.go VectorSearch appends the server-built source_scope_ids predicate to the same bool filter the lucene engine applies during the graph walk. Dropping that append (the weakening) leaves a query that still filters by tenant and embedding profile and still returns well-formed hits, so nothing looks broken -- it simply ranks the whole tenant corpus and lets post-authorization discard the foreign part afterwards, which on a large tenant crowds a workspace's own best passages out of its k nearest neighbours and turns a wrong answer into an empty one. TestVectorSearchAppliesScopeAndVersionStateBeforeRanking asserts the built query carries exactly the authorized scope set, so it kills the mutant.
baseline_meaning: On the unmutated tree VectorSearch builds four filter clauses -- tenant, embedding profile, source scope set and version state -- and the test reads them back out of the serialized request body.
mutant_meaning: With the scope predicate never appended the request carries only three clauses and the scope set is absent, so the assertion on the authorized scope set fails: exactly the declared RED negative control (a retrieval scope filter must be server-built and present, never optional), so the mutant is killed by the registered probe and not vacuous.
runner: tests/contracts/mutation-runner/main.go executes this case from tests/contracts/mutation-registry.json under the GO_UNIT harness for the invariant entry `acceptance.search.client-supplied-scope-filter`; the identical case is committed both here and in the registry so the proof is pinned to the product guard.
